text.zh: Which of the following is the core focus of the Social (S) dimension in the ESG framework?
Corporate carbon emission reduction
Corporate treatment of employees, communities and stakeholders
Corporate board independence
Corporate waste disposal

explanation.zh: *The Social (S) dimension of ESG mainly focuses on how enterprises treat employees, communities, customers, suppliers and other stakeholders, and the impact of their operations on society. A and D belong to the Environmental (E) dimension, and C belongs to the Governance (G) dimension.

text.zh: Which of the following is NOT a key indicator of the Social (S) dimension?
Employee turnover rate
Customer satisfaction
Carbon emission intensity
Community contribution

explanation.zh: *Carbon emission intensity is a core indicator of the Environmental (E) dimension, reflecting the efficiency of corporate carbon emission reduction. A, B, and D are all key indicators of the Social (S) dimension, involving employee management, customer management and community responsibility.

text.zh: What does "employee welfare" in the Social (S) dimension mainly refer to?
The salary paid by the enterprise to employees
A series of benefits provided by the enterprise to employees in addition to wages, including insurance, leave and subsidies
The training opportunities provided by the enterprise to employees
The promotion mechanism of the enterprise

explanation.zh: *Employee welfare refers to the non-wage benefits provided by enterprises to employees to improve their quality of life and work satisfaction, including social insurance, supplementary commercial insurance, paid leave, transportation subsidies, etc. A is employee salary, C and D are part of employee development, not the core of welfare.

text.zh: Which of the following belongs to the content of employee rights protection in the Social (S) dimension?
Enterprises force employees to work overtime without compensation
Enterprises sign labor contracts with employees in accordance with the law
Enterprises refuse to pay employees' social insurance
Enterprises discriminate against employees in terms of salary

explanation.zh: *Signing labor contracts in accordance with the law is an important part of protecting employees' legitimate rights and interests, which can clarify the rights and obligations of both parties. A, C, and D are all acts that violate employees' rights and interests and do not conform to the requirements of the Social (S) dimension.

text.zh: What is the main purpose of corporate employee training?
Reduce employee salaries
Improve employees' professional skills and comprehensive quality to promote enterprise development
Increase employee workload
Replace old employees with new ones

explanation.zh: *The core purpose of employee training is to improve employees' professional skills, professional quality and adaptability, so as to better meet the needs of enterprise development and achieve win-win results between employees and enterprises. A, C, and D are not the purpose of employee training.

text.zh: Which of the following is an example of workplace discrimination?
Enterprises recruit employees based on professional ability
Enterprises refuse to recruit female employees on the ground of "unsuitable for the post"
Enterprises provide the same salary for employees with the same ability and position
Enterprises arrange posts according to employees' strengths

explanation.zh: *Workplace discrimination refers to the unfair treatment of employees in recruitment, salary, promotion and other aspects due to factors such as gender, age, race and disability that are not related to work ability. B is gender discrimination, which belongs to workplace discrimination. A, C, and D are fair employment practices.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "equal pay for equal work" in the workplace?
All employees in the enterprise get the same salary
Employees with the same position, same working ability and same work performance get the same salary
Employees get salary according to their working hours regardless of their ability
Employees get salary according to their seniority regardless of their work performance

explanation.zh: *"Equal pay for equal work" means that in the same enterprise, employees who are engaged in the same work, have the same work ability and achieve the same work performance should receive the same or similar labor remuneration, which reflects the fairness of the workplace. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of "equal pay for equal work".

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to improve employee satisfaction?
Reducing employee rest time
Providing a safe and comfortable working environment
Increasing employee workload without increasing salary
Ignoring employees' opinions and suggestions

explanation.zh: *Providing a safe, comfortable and harmonious working environment can effectively improve employees' work experience and satisfaction. A, C, and D will reduce employee satisfaction and even cause employee turnover.

text.zh: What is the impact of high employee turnover rate on enterprises?
Reducing enterprise recruitment costs
Improving enterprise work efficiency
Increasing enterprise training costs and affecting team stability
Promoting enterprise innovation

explanation.zh: *High employee turnover rate means that enterprises need to continuously recruit and train new employees, which will increase recruitment and training costs, and at the same time affect the stability of the team and the continuity of work. A, B, and D are opposite to the actual impact of high turnover rate.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator of employee health and safety management?
Employee salary level
Number of workplace safety training sessions
Employee promotion opportunities
Employee annual leave days

explanation.zh: *The number of workplace safety training sessions is an important indicator of employee health and safety management, which reflects the enterprise's attention to employee safety and the effectiveness of safety education. A, C, and D are not directly related to health and safety management.

text.zh: What is the core requirement of enterprise occupational health and safety management?
Ensure that employees do not have any work-related injuries
Identify and eliminate workplace safety hazards to protect employees' physical and mental health
Reduce safety management costs
Comply with safety regulations only on the surface

explanation.zh: *The core requirement of occupational health and safety management is to identify, assess and eliminate potential safety hazards in the workplace, formulate safety management systems and emergency plans, and protect employees' physical and mental health and personal safety. A is an ideal state, not a core requirement; C and D do not conform to the concept of safety management.

text.zh: Which of the following is a common workplace safety hazard?
Regular safety training for employees
Unsafe operation of equipment and unqualified protective equipment
Clean and tidy working environment
Standardized operation procedures

explanation.zh: *Workplace safety hazards refer to factors that may cause work-related injuries or occupational diseases, such as unsafe equipment operation, unqualified protective equipment, and hidden dangers in the working environment. A, C, and D are measures to prevent safety hazards, not hazards themselves.

text.zh: Which of the following is an example of corporate social responsibility (CSR) in the Social (S) dimension?
Enterprises pursue maximum profits regardless of social impact
Enterprises donate to public welfare causes and support community development
Enterprises discharge pollutants without treatment
Enterprises default on employees' salaries

explanation.zh: *Corporate social responsibility (CSR) refers to the responsibility that enterprises should bear to society while pursuing economic benefits, including public welfare donations, community support, environmental protection, etc. B is a typical CSR behavior. A, C, and D are behaviors that violate social responsibility.

text.zh: What is the relationship between corporate social responsibility (CSR) and the Social (S) dimension of ESG?
CSR and the S dimension are irrelevant
The S dimension of ESG is an important part of CSR
CSR is an important part of the S dimension of ESG
CSR and the S dimension are completely the same

explanation.zh: *The Social (S) dimension of ESG focuses on the social impact of enterprises, while corporate social responsibility (CSR) is a broader concept that includes environmental, social and governance responsibilities. CSR is an important part of the S dimension, and the S dimension is one of the core components of ESG.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to fulfill community responsibility?
Occupy community public resources without compensation
Provide employment opportunities for community residents
Pollute the community environment
Ignore the demands of community residents

explanation.zh: *Fulfilling community responsibility means that enterprises actively participate in community construction, provide employment opportunities, support community public welfare undertakings, and maintain community harmony. B is a positive measure to fulfill community responsibility. A, C, and D are behaviors that damage community interests.

text.zh: What is the impact of enterprises fulfilling social responsibility on their own development?
Reducing enterprise profits
Improving enterprise brand image and enhancing stakeholder trust
Increasing enterprise operating costs and reducing competitiveness
Attracting negative public attention

explanation.zh: *Fulfilling social responsibility can help enterprises establish a good brand image, win the trust of consumers, investors and other stakeholders, and enhance long-term competitiveness. A, C, and D are one-sided understandings; although fulfilling social responsibility may increase short-term costs, it can bring long-term benefits.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator of customer relationship management in the Social (S) dimension?
Corporate carbon emissions
Customer complaint handling rate
Employee turnover rate
Board diversity

explanation.zh: *Customer complaint handling rate is an important indicator of customer relationship management, reflecting the enterprise's attention to customer needs and the efficiency of solving customer problems. A belongs to the E dimension, C belongs to the S dimension (employee management), and D belongs to the G dimension.

text.zh: What is the core purpose of corporate customer relationship management?
Maximize sales volume regardless of customer interests
Maintain long-term customer relationships and improve customer loyalty
Reduce customer service costs
Ignore customer feedback

explanation.zh: *The core purpose of customer relationship management is to understand customer needs, provide high-quality products and services, solve customer problems in a timely manner, maintain long-term cooperative relationships with customers, and improve customer loyalty and satisfaction. A, C, and D are not the core purpose.

text.zh: Which of the following is an act that damages customer interests?
Providing true product information to customers
Selling counterfeit and shoddy products to customers
Providing after-sales service in accordance with the agreement
Respecting customer privacy

explanation.zh: *Selling counterfeit and shoddy products will damage the interests of customers (such as economic losses, personal safety risks) and violate the requirements of the Social (S) dimension. A, C, and D are acts that protect customer interests.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "customer privacy protection" for enterprises?
Collect customer information at will
Disclose customer personal information to third parties without authorization
Protect customer personal information from being leaked or misused
Ignore customer requirements for privacy protection

explanation.zh: *Customer privacy protection means that enterprises should standardize the collection, storage and use of customer personal information, and prevent customer information from being leaked, misused or sold to protect customer legitimate rights and interests. A, B, and D are acts that violate customer privacy protection.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to protect customer privacy?
Collecting customer information beyond the scope of business needs
Encrypting customer information and establishing a secure storage system
Selling customer information to third parties for profit
Disclosing customer information in public occasions

explanation.zh: *Encrypting customer information and establishing a secure storage system can effectively prevent customer information from being leaked, which is an important measure to protect customer privacy. A, C, and D are acts that damage customer privacy.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator of supplier management in the Social (S) dimension?
Supplier's carbon emission level
Supplier's compliance with labor standards
Supplier's product price
Supplier's delivery speed

explanation.zh: *In the Social (S) dimension, supplier management mainly focuses on whether suppliers comply with labor standards (such as no child labor, no forced labor), environmental protection requirements and ethical norms. A belongs to the E dimension, C and D are operational indicators of suppliers, not social indicators.

text.zh: What is the core requirement of corporate supplier social responsibility management?
Choose suppliers with the lowest price regardless of their social responsibility performance
Supervise suppliers to comply with labor, environmental and ethical standards
Ignore the social responsibility performance of suppliers
Force suppliers to reduce costs at the expense of social responsibility

explanation.zh: *The core requirement of supplier social responsibility management is to establish a supplier evaluation system that includes social responsibility indicators, supervise suppliers to comply with relevant labor standards, environmental regulations and ethical norms, and promote the whole supply chain to fulfill social responsibility. A, C, and D do not conform to the requirement.

text.zh: Which of the following is an unethical behavior of suppliers that enterprises should avoid?
Suppliers provide high-quality products in accordance with the agreement
Suppliers use child labor in production
Suppliers comply with environmental protection regulations
Suppliers pay employees in accordance with the law

explanation.zh: *Using child labor is an unethical behavior that violates labor standards and social morality, and enterprises should avoid cooperating with such suppliers. A, C, and D are ethical behaviors of suppliers.

text.zh: What is the impact of poor supplier social responsibility performance on enterprises?
Improving enterprise brand image
Reducing enterprise legal risks
Bringing reputation risks and legal liabilities to enterprises
Enhancing enterprise competitiveness

explanation.zh: *If the supplier's social responsibility performance is poor (such as using child labor, polluting the environment), it will be associated with the enterprise, leading to the enterprise's reputation damage, and even legal liabilities if it violates relevant regulations. A, B, and D are opposite to the actual impact.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to manage supplier social responsibility?
Signing a social responsibility agreement with suppliers
Ignoring the social responsibility behavior of suppliers
Choosing suppliers only based on product quality
Reducing the supervision of suppliers

explanation.zh: *Signing a social responsibility agreement with suppliers can clarify the social responsibility requirements that suppliers need to meet, and is an effective measure to manage supplier social responsibility. B, C, and D are not effective management measures.

text.zh: What does "human rights protection" in the Social (S) dimension of ESG refer to?
Only protecting the rights of enterprise employees
Protecting the basic human rights of all stakeholders related to the enterprise, including employees, suppliers, customers and communities
Ignoring the human rights of vulnerable groups
Only protecting the rights of enterprise investors

explanation.zh: *Human rights protection in the ESG Social (S) dimension is a broad concept, which requires enterprises to respect and protect the basic human rights of all stakeholders, including the right to work, the right to safety, the right to privacy, etc. A, C, and D are one-sided understandings.

text.zh: Which of the following is an act that violates human rights in enterprise operations?
Providing equal employment opportunities for all employees
Forcing employees to work overtime for a long time without rest
Respecting the religious beliefs of employees
Protecting the personal safety of employees

explanation.zh: *Forcing employees to work overtime for a long time without rest violates the employees' right to rest and is an act that violates human rights. A, C, and D are acts that respect and protect human rights.

text.zh: Which of the following enterprises is most likely to face human rights risks?
Software development enterprise
Textile enterprise that outsources production to areas with weak labor supervision
Financial consulting enterprise
Online retail enterprise

explanation.zh: *Textile enterprises that outsource production to areas with weak labor supervision may face risks such as child labor, forced labor and low wages in the outsourcing factory, which are typical human rights risks. A, C, and D have relatively low human rights risks.

text.zh: What is the measure for enterprises to avoid human rights risks?
Establishing a human rights management system and conducting regular human rights audits
Ignoring the human rights status of the supply chain
Pursuing profits at the expense of human rights
Reducing investment in human rights protection

explanation.zh: *Establishing a human rights management system, formulating human rights policies, and conducting regular human rights audits on the enterprise itself and the supply chain can effectively identify and avoid human rights risks. B, C, and D will increase human rights risks.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator of community impact assessment in the Social (S) dimension?
Enterprise's water consumption
Community residents' satisfaction with the enterprise
Enterprise's board structure
Enterprise's product sales volume

explanation.zh: *Community residents' satisfaction with the enterprise is an important indicator of community impact assessment, reflecting the positive or negative impact of the enterprise's operations on the community. A belongs to the E dimension, C belongs to the G dimension, and D is an economic indicator.

text.zh: What is the purpose of enterprise community impact assessment?
Ignore the impact of the enterprise on the community
Identify the positive and negative impacts of the enterprise on the community and formulate improvement measures
Reduce the enterprise's investment in the community
Avoid communicating with the community

explanation.zh: *The purpose of community impact assessment is to systematically evaluate the positive (such as providing employment, supporting public welfare) and negative (such as environmental pollution, noise interference) impacts of the enterprise's operations on the community, and formulate corresponding measures to strengthen positive impacts and reduce negative impacts. A, C, and D are not the purpose.

text.zh: Which of the following is a positive impact of enterprises on the community?
Polluting the community's air and water
Providing employment opportunities for community residents and promoting local economic development
Occupying community public space
Causing noise pollution to the community

explanation.zh: *Providing employment opportunities for community residents, supporting community public welfare undertakings, and promoting local economic development are all positive impacts of enterprises on the community. A, C, and D are negative impacts.

text.zh: How can enterprises reduce the negative impact on the community?
Strengthen environmental protection measures to reduce pollution
Ignore the community's demands for environmental protection
Expand production scale regardless of community impact
Reduce communication with community residents

explanation.zh: *Strengthening environmental protection measures, reducing air, water and noise pollution, and standardizing production operations can effectively reduce the negative impact of enterprises on the community. B, C, and D will increase the negative impact.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to communicate with the community?
Refusing to hold community communication meetings
Establishing a community communication mechanism to listen to residents' opinions
Hiding the enterprise's production and operation information from the community
Ignoring the community's suggestions for improvement

explanation.zh: *Establishing a community communication mechanism (such as holding communication meetings, setting up feedback channels) to listen to the opinions and suggestions of community residents is an important measure for enterprises to communicate with the community. A, C, and D are acts that block community communication.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "diversity and inclusion" in the workplace?
Recruiting only employees of the same gender and age
Respecting and accepting employees of different genders, ages, races, religions, and abilities, and providing equal development opportunities
Discriminating against employees with different backgrounds
Promoting only employees with the same educational background

explanation.zh: *Workplace diversity and inclusion refer to enterprises respecting and accepting employees with different backgrounds (gender, age, race, religion, disability, etc.), eliminating discrimination, and providing equal employment, training and promotion opportunities for all employees. A, C, and D are opposite to the concept of diversity and inclusion.

text.zh: Which of the following is an example of workplace inclusion?
Providing reasonable accommodation for employees with disabilities
Refusing to recruit employees with disabilities
Separating employees of different races in work arrangements
Giving preferential treatment to employees of a certain gender

explanation.zh: *Providing reasonable accommodation for employees with disabilities (such as barrier-free facilities, adjusted work arrangements) is a typical example of workplace inclusion, which helps employees with disabilities better complete their work. B, C, and D are acts of exclusion and discrimination.

text.zh: What is the benefit of enterprises promoting workplace diversity and inclusion?
Reducing team innovation ability
Improving employee satisfaction and team cohesion
Increasing workplace conflicts
Reducing enterprise competitiveness

explanation.zh: *Promoting workplace diversity and inclusion can make employees feel respected and valued, improve work satisfaction and loyalty, and at the same time bring different perspectives and ideas to the team, enhance innovation ability and competitiveness. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual benefits.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to promote workplace diversity and inclusion?
Formulating anti-discrimination policies and conducting diversity training
Maintaining a single team structure
Discriminating against employees with different backgrounds
Ignoring the needs of vulnerable groups of employees

explanation.zh: *Formulating anti-discrimination policies, conducting diversity and inclusion training for employees, and establishing a fair evaluation and promotion mechanism are effective measures to promote workplace diversity and inclusion. B, C, and D are not conducive to promoting diversity and inclusion.

text.zh: What is the core content of enterprise labor relations management?
Controlling employee wages and reducing labor costs
Establishing a harmonious and stable labor relationship between enterprises and employees
Forcing employees to accept unreasonable working conditions
Ignoring employees' legitimate demands

explanation.zh: *The core content of labor relations management is to standardize the rights and obligations of both enterprises and employees, resolve labor disputes in a timely manner, and establish a harmonious, stable and mutually beneficial labor relationship. A, C, and D are acts that damage labor relations.

text.zh: Which of the following is a way to resolve labor disputes between enterprises and employees?
Enterprises unilaterally terminate labor contracts without reason
Negotiation, mediation, arbitration and litigation
Ignoring employees' appeals
Threatening employees to give up their legitimate rights and interests

explanation.zh: *The legal ways to resolve labor disputes include negotiation between both parties, mediation by trade unions or labor dispute mediation committees, arbitration by labor dispute arbitration commissions, and litigation by people's courts. A, C, and D are illegal ways to handle labor disputes.

text.zh: What is the impact of harmonious labor relations on enterprises?
Increasing employee turnover rate
Reducing enterprise work efficiency
Improving employee loyalty and reducing labor disputes
Increasing enterprise operating costs

explanation.zh: *Harmonious labor relations can make employees have a sense of belonging and loyalty, reduce labor disputes and employee turnover, and improve work efficiency and enterprise stability. A, B, and D are opposite to the actual impact.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to maintain harmonious labor relations?
Signing labor contracts with employees in accordance with the law and paying wages on time
Defaulting on employees' wages and social insurance
Refusing to negotiate with employees on labor issues
Violating labor laws and regulations

explanation.zh: *Signing labor contracts in accordance with the law, paying wages and social insurance on time, and respecting employees' legitimate rights and interests are important measures to maintain harmonious labor relations. B, C, and D are acts that damage labor relations.

text.zh: What does "product safety" in the Social (S) dimension refer to?
The product is cheap and affordable
The product meets national safety standards and will not cause harm to consumers' personal and property safety
The product has a beautiful appearance
The product has a long service life

explanation.zh: *Product safety in the Social (S) dimension refers to the fact that enterprise products meet national and industry safety standards, do not contain harmful substances, and will not cause harm to consumers' personal health and property safety during use. A, C, and D are not the core of product safety.

text.zh: Which of the following is an act that violates product safety requirements?
Conducting strict quality inspection on products before they leave the factory
Selling products that do not meet safety standards
Providing product safety instructions to consumers
Recalling unqualified products in a timely manner

explanation.zh: *Selling products that do not meet safety standards (such as food with excessive additives, electrical products with potential safety hazards) will endanger consumers' personal and property safety, which is an act that violates product safety requirements. A, C, and D are acts that ensure product safety.

text.zh: What is the responsibility of enterprises for product safety?
Ignore product safety issues and focus only on sales volume
Establish a product quality and safety management system to ensure product safety
Shift the responsibility for product safety to consumers
Hide product safety hazards from consumers

explanation.zh: *Enterprises are the main responsible subjects for product safety, and need to establish a complete product quality and safety management system, conduct strict quality inspection, and take timely measures to recall unqualified products to ensure product safety. A, C, and D are acts that shirk product safety responsibility.

text.zh: What is the impact of product safety incidents on enterprises?
Improving enterprise brand reputation
Reducing consumer trust and facing legal liabilities
Increasing product sales volume
Enhancing enterprise competitiveness

explanation.zh: *Product safety incidents (such as food safety accidents, electrical product safety hazards) will damage consumers' trust in the enterprise, lead to a decline in product sales, and even make the enterprise face legal liabilities such as fines and compensation. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual impact.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to ensure product safety?
Establishing a product quality inspection mechanism
Reducing product quality inspection costs
Using unqualified raw materials to reduce production costs
Ignoring product safety standards

explanation.zh: *Establishing a strict product quality inspection mechanism, conducting full-process inspection of raw materials, production processes and finished products, can effectively ensure product safety. B, C, and D will reduce product safety and increase safety risks.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "ethical business conduct" in the Social (S) dimension?
Enterprises pursue profits through improper means such as fraud and bribery
Enterprises conduct business activities in accordance with laws, regulations and moral norms, and do not engage in unethical behaviors
Enterprises ignore the interests of stakeholders to maximize their own profits
Enterprises engage in false advertising to promote products

explanation.zh: *Ethical business conduct refers to enterprises abiding by national laws and regulations, adhering to business ethics, and conducting business activities in a fair, honest and responsible manner, without engaging in fraud, bribery, false advertising and other unethical behaviors. A, C, and D are unethical business conducts.

text.zh: Which of the following is an unethical business conduct?
Honest transaction with customers and suppliers
Providing true and accurate product information to consumers
Bribery of government officials to obtain business opportunities
Complying with market competition rules

explanation.zh: *Bribery of government officials to obtain business opportunities is an unethical and illegal business conduct, which violates market rules and social morality. A, B, and D are ethical business conducts.

text.zh: What is the benefit of enterprises adhering to ethical business conduct?
Gaining short-term benefits but losing long-term trust
Establishing a good corporate image and enhancing long-term competitiveness
Reducing enterprise operating costs
Avoiding market competition

explanation.zh: *Adhering to ethical business conduct can help enterprises gain the trust of consumers, investors and other stakeholders, establish a good brand image, and enhance long-term competitiveness. A, C, and D are not the benefits of ethical business conduct.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to strengthen ethical management?
Formulating a code of business ethics and conducting ethical training for employees
Ignoring unethical behaviors of employees
Encouraging employees to pursue profits through any means
Hiding unethical business behaviors from the public

explanation.zh: *Formulating a code of business ethics, clarifying ethical norms for employees, and conducting regular ethical training can help employees establish ethical awareness and standardize business behaviors. B, C, and D are not conducive to strengthening ethical management.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator of enterprise social performance in the Social (S) dimension?
Enterprise's carbon emission reduction volume
Employee training hours per capita
Enterprise's return on investment (ROI)
Enterprise's board size

explanation.zh: *Employee training hours per capita is an important indicator of enterprise social performance, reflecting the enterprise's attention to employee development and investment in human resources. A belongs to the E dimension, C is an economic indicator, and D belongs to the G dimension.

text.zh: How do enterprises measure and evaluate social performance?
Ignoring social performance indicators and focusing only on economic benefits
Establishing a social performance evaluation system to track indicators such as employee welfare, customer satisfaction and community contribution
Falsifying social performance data to meet external requirements
Only evaluating social performance based on public praise

explanation.zh: *Enterprises need to establish a scientific social performance evaluation system, select key indicators (such as employee turnover rate, customer complaint handling rate, public welfare donation amount), track and analyze data, and comprehensively evaluate social performance. A, C, and D are unscientific evaluation methods.

text.zh: What is the role of evaluating enterprise social performance?
To meet the requirements of regulators perfunctorily
To identify the advantages and disadvantages of social responsibility performance and promote continuous improvement
To reduce the enterprise's investment in social responsibility
To hide the enterprise's poor social performance

explanation.zh: *Evaluating social performance can help enterprises clearly understand their own advantages and disadvantages in fulfilling social responsibility, find existing problems, and formulate improvement measures to continuously improve social performance. A, C, and D are not the role of social performance evaluation.

text.zh: Which of the following is an example of enterprise social performance improvement?
Reducing employee training investment
Improving customer complaint handling rate from 80% to 95%
Reducing public welfare donations
Ignoring employee safety and health

explanation.zh: *Improving the customer complaint handling rate means that the enterprise is more efficient in solving customer problems, which is an improvement in social performance (customer management). A, C, and D are all declines in social performance.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "stakeholder engagement" in the Social (S) dimension?
Enterprises only pay attention to the interests of investors and ignore other stakeholders
Enterprises communicate and interact with all stakeholders (employees, customers, suppliers, communities, etc.) to understand their needs and opinions
Enterprises refuse to communicate with stakeholders
Enterprises only communicate with stakeholders when there is a problem

explanation.zh: *Stakeholder engagement refers to enterprises taking the initiative to communicate and interact with all stakeholders, understand their needs, opinions and expectations, and take these into account in business decision-making to achieve balanced development of stakeholder interests. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of stakeholder engagement.

text.zh: Which of the following is a stakeholder of an enterprise?
Only enterprise investors
Only enterprise employees
Employees, customers, suppliers, communities, investors and other groups related to the enterprise
Only enterprise customers

explanation.zh: *Stakeholders of an enterprise refer to all groups or individuals that are affected by the enterprise's operations or can affect the enterprise's operations, including investors, employees, customers, suppliers, communities, government departments, etc. A, B, and D are only part of the stakeholders.

text.zh: What is the purpose of enterprise stakeholder engagement?
Ignore the needs of stakeholders to maximize their own profits
Build good relationships with stakeholders and promote the sustainable development of the enterprise
Reduce the enterprise's communication costs
Avoid the demands of stakeholders

explanation.zh: *The purpose of stakeholder engagement is to build trust and good relationships with stakeholders, understand their needs and expectations, resolve potential conflicts, and promote the long-term sustainable development of the enterprise. A, C, and D are not the purpose.

text.zh: Which of the following is a way for enterprises to engage with stakeholders?
Holding stakeholder forums and collecting opinions
Refusing to respond to stakeholders' inquiries
Hiding enterprise information from stakeholders
Ignoring stakeholders' suggestions

explanation.zh: *Holding stakeholder forums, setting up feedback channels, and publishing social responsibility reports are all effective ways for enterprises to engage with stakeholders. B, C, and D are acts that block stakeholder engagement.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator of employee development in the Social (S) dimension?
Employee salary level
Employee promotion rate
Enterprise's energy consumption
Product sales volume

explanation.zh: *Employee promotion rate is an important indicator of employee development, reflecting the enterprise's promotion mechanism and the space for employee growth. A is an indicator of employee welfare, C belongs to the E dimension, and D is an economic indicator.

text.zh: What is the measure for enterprises to promote employee development?
Providing regular training and establishing a fair promotion mechanism
Refusing to provide training opportunities for employees
Promoting employees only based on seniority
Ignoring employees' career development needs

explanation.zh: *Providing regular professional training, skill training and management training for employees, and establishing a fair promotion mechanism based on ability and performance can effectively promote employee development. B, C, and D are not conducive to employee development.

text.zh: What is the impact of employee development on enterprises?
Increasing employee turnover rate
Improving employee professional ability and enterprise work efficiency
Reducing enterprise operating costs
Increasing workplace conflicts

explanation.zh: *Promoting employee development can improve employees' professional skills and comprehensive quality, enhance work efficiency and innovation ability, and at the same time improve employee loyalty and reduce turnover rate. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual impact.

text.zh: Which of the following is an example of employee career development support provided by enterprises?
Formulating personalized career plans for employees
Ignoring employees' career development needs
Refusing to provide training for employees' career development
Limiting employees' career development space

explanation.zh: *Formulating personalized career plans for employees, providing targeted training and guidance, and creating a good career development environment are examples of enterprises supporting employee career development. B, C, and D are acts that hinder employee career development.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "work-life balance" for employees?
Working overtime for a long time to complete work tasks
Balancing work and personal life, ensuring sufficient rest and family time while completing work tasks
Ignoring work tasks and focusing only on personal life
Working without rest to pursue career development

explanation.zh: *Work-life balance refers to employees being able to balance the relationship between work and personal life, complete work tasks efficiently, and at the same time have sufficient time to rest, accompany family and engage in personal hobbies, so as to maintain physical and mental health. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of work-life balance.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to help employees achieve work-life balance?
Encouraging employees to work overtime without compensation
Implementing a flexible working system and providing paid leave
Increasing employee workload
Ignoring employees' needs for rest

explanation.zh: *Implementing a flexible working system (such as flexible working hours, remote work), providing sufficient paid leave, and avoiding unnecessary overtime are effective measures to help employees achieve work-life balance. A, C, and D will damage work-life balance.

text.zh: What is the benefit of employees achieving work-life balance?
Reducing work efficiency
Improving physical and mental health and work satisfaction
Increasing workplace conflicts
Reducing employee loyalty

explanation.zh: *Employees who achieve work-life balance can maintain good physical and mental health, reduce work pressure, improve work satisfaction and loyalty, and thus improve work efficiency. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual benefits.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator of customer satisfaction in the Social (S) dimension?
Customer repurchase rate
Enterprise's carbon emissions
Employee turnover rate
Board diversity

explanation.zh: *Customer repurchase rate is an important indicator of customer satisfaction, reflecting the degree of customer recognition of the enterprise's products and services. A high repurchase rate indicates high customer satisfaction. B belongs to the E dimension, C belongs to the S dimension (employee management), and D belongs to the G dimension.

text.zh: How do enterprises improve customer satisfaction?
Providing low-quality products and services
Listening to customer feedback and continuously improving products and services
Ignoring customer complaints
Increasing product prices arbitrarily

explanation.zh: *Listening to customer feedback, solving customer problems in a timely manner, improving product quality and service level, and providing personalized services can effectively improve customer satisfaction. A, C, and D will reduce customer satisfaction.

text.zh: What is the impact of high customer satisfaction on enterprises?
Reducing product sales volume
Improving customer loyalty and increasing market share
Increasing customer complaints
Reducing enterprise competitiveness

explanation.zh: *High customer satisfaction can improve customer loyalty, promote customer repurchase, and attract new customers through word-of-mouth, thereby increasing market share and enterprise competitiveness. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual impact.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to collect customer feedback?
Setting up customer feedback hotlines and online feedback channels
Refusing to accept customer feedback
Ignoring customer suggestions
Hiding customer feedback information

explanation.zh: *Setting up customer feedback hotlines, online feedback platforms, and conducting customer surveys are effective ways to collect customer feedback. B, C, and D are acts that ignore customer feedback.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "supply chain social responsibility" in the Social (S) dimension?
Enterprises only pay attention to their own social responsibility and ignore the social responsibility of suppliers
Enterprises promote the whole supply chain to fulfill social responsibility, including suppliers, distributors and other partners
Enterprises force suppliers to reduce costs regardless of social responsibility
Enterprises ignore the social responsibility performance of the supply chain

explanation.zh: *Supply chain social responsibility refers to enterprises not only fulfilling their own social responsibility, but also guiding and supervising suppliers, distributors and other partners in the supply chain to comply with labor standards, environmental regulations and ethical norms, and promote the sustainable development of the whole supply chain. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to promote supply chain social responsibility?
Establishing a supply chain social responsibility evaluation system
Ignoring the social responsibility performance of suppliers
Choosing suppliers only based on product price
Reducing the supervision of suppliers

explanation.zh: *Establishing a supply chain social responsibility evaluation system, incorporating social responsibility indicators into supplier selection and evaluation, and conducting regular audits of suppliers are effective measures to promote supply chain social responsibility. B, C, and D are not effective measures.

text.zh: What is the risk of ignoring supply chain social responsibility?
Improving enterprise brand image
Reducing enterprise legal risks
Bringing reputation risks and legal liabilities to enterprises
Enhancing enterprise competitiveness

explanation.zh: *If enterprises ignore the social responsibility performance of the supply chain (such as suppliers using child labor, polluting the environment), it will affect the enterprise's brand reputation, and even lead to legal liabilities if it violates relevant regulations. A, B, and D are opposite to the actual risks.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator of supply chain social responsibility?
Supplier's product quality
Supplier's compliance with labor standards
Supplier's delivery speed
Supplier's product price

explanation.zh: *Supplier's compliance with labor standards (such as no child labor, no forced labor, fair wages) is a key indicator of supply chain social responsibility. A, C, and D are operational indicators of suppliers, not social responsibility indicators.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "community investment" in the Social (S) dimension?
Enterprises invest in the community to obtain immediate economic benefits
Enterprises invest resources (funds, technology, personnel) in the community to promote community development and improve residents' quality of life
Enterprises occupy community resources without investment
Enterprises invest in the community only to meet regulatory requirements

explanation.zh: *Community investment refers to enterprises taking the initiative to invest funds, technology, personnel and other resources in the community, such as supporting community public welfare undertakings, building public facilities, and providing skills training for residents, to promote community development and improve residents' quality of life. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of community investment.

text.zh: Which of the following is an example of enterprise community investment?
Donating funds to build community schools and hospitals
Occupying community public space for production
Polluting the community environment
Ignoring the community's development needs

explanation.zh: *Donating funds to build community schools, hospitals, public green spaces and other public facilities is a typical example of community investment, which can promote community development and improve residents' quality of life. B, C, and D are acts that damage community interests.

text.zh: What is the benefit of enterprise community investment?
Reducing enterprise profits
Improving the relationship between the enterprise and the community and enhancing brand influence
Increasing enterprise operating costs
Attracting negative public attention

explanation.zh: *Community investment can help enterprises build a good relationship with the community, gain the recognition and support of community residents, enhance brand influence and social image, and create a good development environment for the enterprise. A, C, and D are one-sided understandings.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator of enterprise community investment?
Enterprise's community investment amount
Enterprise's carbon emissions
Employee turnover rate
Product sales volume

explanation.zh: *Enterprise's community investment amount (such as public welfare donation amount, investment in community projects) is an important indicator of community investment, reflecting the enterprise's investment in the community. B belongs to the E dimension, C belongs to the S dimension (employee management), and D is an economic indicator.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "anti-corruption" in the Social (S) dimension of ESG?
Enterprises turn a blind eye to corruption behaviors of employees
Enterprises establish anti-corruption systems to prevent and combat corruption behaviors in business activities
Enterprises encourage employees to engage in corruption to obtain business opportunities
Enterprises cover up corruption behaviors of employees

explanation.zh: *Anti-corruption in the ESG Social (S) dimension refers to enterprises establishing a sound anti-corruption system, formulating anti-corruption policies, strengthening anti-corruption education for employees, and preventing and combating corruption behaviors such as bribery and embezzlement in business activities. A, C, and D are opposite to the concept of anti-corruption.

text.zh: Which of the following is an anti-corruption measure for enterprises?
Establishing an anti-corruption complaint mechanism and investigating corruption behaviors
Ignoring corruption behaviors of employees
Covering up corruption behaviors of senior management
Encouraging employees to accept bribes

explanation.zh: *Establishing an anti-corruption complaint mechanism, conducting regular anti-corruption training, and investigating and punishing corruption behaviors are effective anti-corruption measures. B, C, and D are acts that encourage or condone corruption.

text.zh: What is the impact of corruption on enterprises?
Improving enterprise operating efficiency
Damaging enterprise reputation and facing legal liabilities
Enhancing enterprise competitiveness
Reducing enterprise operating costs

explanation.zh: *Corruption behaviors (such as bribery, embezzlement) will damage the enterprise's brand reputation, disrupt the normal business order, and make the enterprise face legal liabilities such as fines and criminal penalties. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual impact.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator of enterprise anti-corruption performance?
Number of anti-corruption training sessions
Enterprise's carbon emissions
Employee salary level
Product sales volume

explanation.zh: *The number of anti-corruption training sessions is an important indicator of enterprise anti-corruption performance, reflecting the enterprise's attention to anti-corruption and the effectiveness of anti-corruption education. B belongs to the E dimension, C is an employee welfare indicator, and D is an economic indicator.
